finding.summary: The docs slim toolbar's color-reset change (`""` → `undefined`) — the exact wiring issue #728 is about — ships with no test; only the sibling `TextFormatGroup` got one.
finding.evidence: The new UI regression test `packages/frontend/tests/components/text-formatting/color-reset.test.ts` renders only `TextFormatGroup`. `docs-formatting-toolbar.tsx` contains its own `handleTextColor` / `handleHighlightColor` and its own `onReset={() => handleTextColor(undefined)}` (lines ~402, 490, 512) and there is no test file for it: `Glob packages/frontend/tests/**/*formatting-toolbar*` returns nothing, and grepping `.test.*` files for `docs-formatting-toolbar` finds no match. verdict.reason: The docs slim toolbar's issue-#728 fix is genuinely untested. `docs-formatting-toolbar.tsx:402-414` defines its own `handleTextColor`/`handleHighlightColor` and wires them at lines 490/512 as `onReset={() => handleTextColor(undefined)}`, but no test renders or imports `DocsFormattingToolbar`: grepping `DocsFormattingToolbar|docs-formatting-toolbar` across all .ts/.tsx yields only src importers (docs-detail.tsx:28, shared-document.tsx:40, harness/hunt/page.tsx:38), and no test imports any of those either. The shipped regression test (tests/components/text-formatting/color-reset.test.ts:67) renders only `TextFormatGroup`, and color-picker-grid.test.ts:61,79 exercises the shared grid with a `vi.fn()` onReset — neither can fail if `""` were re-introduced in the docs toolbar. I also followed the indirect chains: the dev-only `/harness/hunt` route mounts the real toolbar (hunt/page.tsx:319), but its oracle script verify-hunt-oracles.mjs:859-860 only selects a swatch and contains no `Reset`/`data-none-control` interaction, hunt-ui-oracles.mjs has no color oracle, verify-interaction-browser.mjs has no applyStyle/color assertions, and the repo has no Playwright config or *.spec.ts. `data-none-control` is clicked in exactly two test files, neither touching the docs toolbar. The task doc (docs/tasks/active/20260812-docs-font-color-reset-todo.md:27-29 vs :100) lists two changed toolbar call sites but only one frontend test, corroborating the gap. Major under the test-adequacy rubric: a changed behavior shipped with no meaningful test covering it.

finding.summary: New slide-inline validation (`assertValidSlideInlines`) ships with no test in the slides arm of the controller spec
finding.evidence: The delta adds `assertValidSlideInlines` (docs-content.controller.ts:711-770) which rejects non-array `inlines`, non-object entries, non-string `text`, and non-object `style` inside every slide text body. The `slides body shape validation` describe block (spec lines 616-1027) has cases for `style.alignment`, `style.marginTop`, `style.lineHeight`, `style.textIndent`, notes, group children, layout placeholders/staticElements, and a positive case that omits `inlines` entirely (line 1008) — but not a single case asserting a malformed inline is rejected through the slides path. The only `inlines: [{ text: 5 }]` case (line 536) is the docs arm and asserts `/blocks\[0\]\.inlines\[0\]/`, which the pre-existing docs validator already satisfied, so it cannot fail if the new slides guard is deleted. Nothing in the suite pins the new error paths or the deliberate `undefined/null` tolerance for a *present* but empty inline list.

verdict.reason: The finding claims the new slide-inline validation ships with no test in the slides arm. It does have tests — the reviewer searched for `assertValidSlideInlines` (the function is actually named `normalizeSlideInlines`, controller.ts:752) and read the slides describe block only to line 1027, but that block runs to spec:1149. Lines 1034-1120 contain four dedicated negative tests, one per error path in `normalizeSlideInlines`: non-array `inlines` (spec:1034-1041 → controller.ts:761-764), non-object inline entry (spec:1043-1050 → controller.ts:768-772), non-string `text` (spec:1052-1061 → controller.ts:773-777), non-object `style` (spec:1063-1077 → controller.ts:782-786), plus coverage through the slide-notes and layout-placeholder paths (spec:1079-1120). All use the slides-scoped `expectReject` (spec:617-624) and assert slides-only message paths such as `/elements\[0\]\.data\.blocks\[0\]\.inlines\[0\].*'text'.*string/`, which the docs-arm validator can never emit, so they fail if the new guard is removed. The deliberate absent-value tolerance is also pinned non-vacuously at spec:1122-1148, which asserts on the mutated request body (`blocks[0].inlines` becomes `[]`, `blocks[1].inlines[0].style` becomes `{}`) rather than on a mock call.

finding.summary: `toHeadingStyleId` sanitization of `headingLevel` into `<w:pStyle w:val>` has no test
finding.evidence: The delta replaces `if (headingLevel) parts.push(`<w:pStyle w:val="Heading${headingLevel}"/>`)` with a range-checked `toHeadingStyleId`. packages/docs/test/export/docx-style-map.test.ts contains no occurrence of `headingLevel` or `pStyle` at all (grep returned no matches in that file; the only `Heading1` hit in packages/docs/test is docx-parser.test.ts:145, an import fixture). So nothing asserts that a valid level still emits `Heading3`, that `0`/`7`/`NaN`/`1.5` drop the element, or that a hostile string such as `1"/><w:jc w:val="right` is no longer interpolated — the exact class of test the same file already has for `alignment` (line 149) and colors (lines 78/91). Deleting `toHeadingStyleId` and restoring the raw interpolation would leave the suite green.

verdict.reason: The claimed-missing tests exist in the very file the finding says has no occurrence of `headingLevel` or `pStyle`. packages/docs/test/export/docx-style-map.test.ts:178-213 contains a dedicated `describe('heading level → <w:pStyle w:val>')` block that covers each case the finding enumerates: valid levels 1-6 each emit `<w:pStyle w:val="HeadingN"/>` (lines 183-189), undefined/omitted emits no pStyle (lines 191-194), the out-of-range and non-integer set `[0, -1, 7, 99, 1.5, NaN, Infinity]` drops the element (lines 196-200), and the hostile string `'1"/><w:pStyle w:val="Evil'` plus a `'constructor'` prototype-chain value are neither interpolated nor emitted (lines 202-212). The tests are non-vacuous: they invoke the real, unmocked `buildParagraphPropertiesXml` (imported at lines 2-6) and assert on its returned XML, so removing `toHeadingStyleId` (src/export/docx-style-map.ts:139-144) and restoring raw interpolation would emit `<w:pStyle w:val="NaN"/>` and the `Evil` fragment, failing lines 198 and 208-209 — the opposite of the finding's stated falsification test. The finding's factual premise is therefore wrong, not merely differently weighted.

finding.summary: `toSrgbHex` now routes theme colors through `toRgbHexColor` with a black fallback — untested, and the existing theme test mirrors the OLD implementation
finding.evidence: packages/slides/test/export/pptx/theme.test.ts only ever calls `themeToXml(defaultLight, 1)`; every color assertion uses well-formed `#RRGGBB` values. Its round-trip test (lines 63-79) recomputes the expected value with `h.replace(/^#/, '').toUpperCase()` — literally the old `toSrgbHex` body — so it passes identically before and after the change and cannot detect a regression in the new normalizer. No test feeds a theme color that `toRgbHexColor` rejects (e.g. `'#FFF"/><a:srgbClr val="000000'`, `'rgb(1,2,3)'`, `''`) to pin either the injection-free `[0-9A-F]{6}` guarantee or the documented `'000000'` degradation.

verdict.reason: The finding claims no test feeds a theme color that `toRgbHexColor` rejects and that nothing pins either the `[0-9A-F]{6}` injection-free guarantee or the `'000000'` degradation. The same file the reviewer says they read in full contains `describe('clrScheme slot normalization')` (theme.test.ts:93-127), which does all of it: a `withColor()` helper (lines 98-101) injects arbitrary strings into `theme.colors.accent1`, refuting the 'only ever calls themeToXml(defaultLight, 1)' claim; lines 103-107 assert `'#f00' -> val="FF0000"`, `'1a73e8' -> val="1A73E8"` and `'rgb(255, 0, 0)' -> val="FF0000"`, all of which FAIL under the old `h.replace(/^#/,'').toUpperCase()` body (which would emit `F00` and `RGB(255, 0, 0)`), so they are discriminating rather than mirroring the old implementation; lines 109-115 pin the documented black degradation for `''`, `'not-a-color'`, `'transparent'`; lines 117-126 use the hostile value `'FF0000"/><a:custom val="pwned'`, assert `val="000000"`, `not.toContain('pwned')`, and loop every emitted `<a:srgbClr val="...">` asserting `/^[0-9A-F]{6}$/` — the exact guarantee said to be unpinned. The test is not over-mocked (no `vi.mock`/`vi.fn` in the file) and drives the real `toRgbHexColor` at packages/docs/src/model/color.ts:113-143, whose shorthand-expansion and `rgb()` branches are what make the assertions non-vacuous. The reviewer's sub-observation that the round-trip test (lines 63-79) recomputes expectations with the old formula is accurate but is redundancy, not a coverage gap, given the dedicated block above.

finding.summary: The Record→Map conversions in connector.ts, shape.ts and layout.ts (prototype-chain guard plus a new `?? 'line'` routing fallback) have no tests
finding.evidence: This delta converts `ROUTING_PRST`, `KIND_TO_OOXML`, `SIZE_TO_OOXML` (connector.ts), `DASH_VAL` (shape.ts) and `BUILT_IN_TO_TYPE` (layout.ts) to `Map`s and adds a new `?? 'line'` fallback for unknown routing (previously `prst="undefined"` was emitted). Grepping packages/slides/test/export for `constructor|prototype|hostile|__proto__` returns hits only for `kindToPrst` (shape.test.ts:19-22, added in an earlier round) and text.test.ts:150 — none for routing, arrowhead kind/size, dash or layout id. connector.test.ts only exercises the three legitimate routings and a well-formed arrowhead; shape.test.ts never exercises `stroke.dash`; theme.test.ts only feeds `BUILT_IN_LAYOUTS` ids to `layoutToXml`. Reverting any of these five to the object literal (or dropping the new routing fallback) would keep the suite green, even though the prior round established the `kindToPrst('constructor')` test as the pattern for exactly this change.

verdict.reason:
The finding claims none of the five Record→Map conversions (ROUTING_PRST, KIND_TO_OOXML, SIZE_TO_OOXML, DASH_VAL, BUILT_IN_TO_TYPE) nor the new `?? 'line'` routing fallback are covered. All three files have explicit, non-vacuous tests, and they are exactly in the directory the reviewer says they grepped:

1. connector.test.ts:90-128 — a whole `describe('connector attribute lookups are closed')` block. It.each over ['constructor','toString','__proto__','valueOf','nope'] asserts `prst="line"` and `not.toContain('undefined')`/`'native code'` — this fails if the `?? 'line'` fallback is dropped (object literal would emit `prst="undefined"`) and fails if ROUTING_PRST reverts to an object (`constructor` would stringify native code). A second it.each covers arrowhead kind AND size (KIND_TO_OOXML/SIZE_TO_OOXML) asserting the exact `<a:tailEnd type="triangle" w="med" len="med"/>`. A third test feeds a quote-breaking hostile routing and asserts no `<a:custGeom>`.

2. shape.test.ts:149-179 — `describe('DASH_VAL is a closed lookup')`: maps dashed→`val="dash"`, dotted→`val="sysDot"`, no prstDash for solid, it.each over constructor/toString/__proto__/nope asserting `val="dash"` with no 'native code'/'undefined', plus a hostile `dash"/><a:custom val="pwned` case. This directly contradicts "shape.test.ts never exercises stroke.dash".

3. theme.test.ts:129-150 — `describe('BUILT_IN_TO_TYPE is a closed lookup')`: it.each over constructor/toString/__proto__/my-custom-layout asserting `type="blank"` and no `type="undefined"`/'native code', plus a hostile layout id test. This contradicts "theme.test.ts only feeds BUILT_IN_LAYOUTS ids to layoutToXml".

Reverting any of the five maps to object literals, or dropping the routing fallback, would turn these suites red — the opposite of the finding's assertion.
